publicText: Civic Hall announced the January 30, 2016 constituent-services hackathon for 1-3 p.m. The archived page preserves the evidence in an embedded social feed; no dedicated Civic Hall calendar or event-detail page has been recovered.
caveatOverride: Do not describe the Wayback container as a recovered event-detail or calendar page.

publicText: The New York City Council described the Civic Hall gathering as its first CouncilStat hackathon. This supports the exact phrase "first CouncilStat hackathon," not broader first-hackathon claims.
caveatOverride: Use "first CouncilStat hackathon." Do not broaden the claim into a first-hackathon claim about civic data, the Council, or Civic Hall.

publicText: Politico New York reported that Jamie attended a Council hackathon at Civic Hall in January before the data release, then created CallNYC after the full dataset became available. The public repository remains a project artifact for the historical implementation.
caveatOverride: CallNYC was independent, archived, unofficial, and historical. Do not call it an official Council product or current civic service.

publicText: Politico New York reported that Council offices used CouncilStat differently and entered information with differing frequency, so the records needed cautious interpretation.
caveatOverride: Do not interpret case counts as a simple measure of office quality, specialization, demand, or service effectiveness.

publicText: Politico New York covered CallNYC on March 14, 2016, in an article by Miranda Neubauer.
caveatOverride: Link the archived PDF and identify the publication and date.

publicText: The CallNYC case study, Politico New York coverage, and the public project repository support using CallNYC as evidence of public-sector data interpretation, bounded resident-facing implementation, and careful treatment of source limitations.
caveatOverride: This supports role-fit evidence for implementation judgment. It does not make CallNYC an official Council product or current civic service.
